headline: Kira was unanimously named next chair, and the May meeting minutes were unanimously approved.
summary: Jordan will step down as chair and stay on as a member. Discussion covered coordinating with the Planning Board on clean energy reviews, a fleet assessment the city does not have yet, and a possible climate leaders program application.
decisions: Approved the minutes from the May meeting unanimously.
Named Kira as next chair, unanimously.

decision_evidence.quote: Review and approve minutes from CEAC May meeting — meeting minutes unanimously approved
Nancy nominates Kira as next CEAC chair, Tom seconded, members unanimously vote in favor.

transcript:
# Clean Energy Advisory Committee

Wednesday, June 17, 2026

6:30 pm - 8:00 pm

Meeting location: Beverly Public Library and Virtual

City of Beverly, received and recorded, City Clerk's Office, 2026 NOV 12 P 12:40

- **Jordan called the meeting to order at 6:35pm**
- **Roll call (see members above)**
  - **CEAC members present** - Jordan Stutt, Nancy Schalch, Sarah Cullinan, Fred Hopps, Kira Fabrizio, Tom Keeley
  - **CEAC members absent** - Amy Smith
  - Other attendees: Bruce, Kevin, David, Ibrahim Lopez-Hernandez, Guy Bellino, Wayne Miller, Julia Long
- **Review and approve minutes from CEAC May meeting - meeting minutes unanimously approved**
  - Note that the AI audio notes we tried last time are best as a back-up record, but we will continue to need and use a human to record minutes
- **City Updates**
  - Fleet assessment - don't have the report yet, will discuss at September meeting
  - Application for climate leaders program possible by August? Don't have a project ready to submit at this point. Julia happy to hear ideas for possible projects.
- **The Bigger Picture**
  - Energy supply and pricing changes as war ends in Iran.
  - Data centers in Ireland required to bring new power online to meet their own demand. Some states doing and considering this.
  - War in Iran expected to impact food supply prices, affect poor around the world.
  - RGGI auction price hit new record high of $35 per ton of carbon - revenue to states, mostly invested in clean energy programs, creates some incentives for clean energy investment.
- **Clean Transportation Update (Kira / Jordan)**
  - Continuing researching models / possibilities and thinking about what fits for Beverly, and initiating conversations within the City, including City Councilors and others. Will report back on findings in September.
- **Coordinating with Planning Board on Clean Energy (Wayne)**
  - Anyone with business before the planning board knows to come prepared, parking, traffic, engineering department weighs in on questions and queries. CEAC could also weigh in on applications, in terms of additional questions that could be asked of applicants. Could think together about how to flesh out a process for this.
  - Next step? Meeting with the planning department - Darlene and Ken - and discuss what might be logistically possible to involve CEAC in review. CEAC members can attend planning board meeting (they are public and happen monthly, Wayne can alert us when there is one coming with some potential topics of interest). Fred volunteered to meet with Darlene about how this might happen. Nancy mentioned that CEAC could develop a check list to be used in project review - something that could even be shared with people in advance.
  - Julia - Resilient Together (Climate Action Plan) does provide a checklist that they use as a tool. Could start with a review of this document to start creating a checklist. Also LEED for cities - Mayor interested in this, and it also offers a checklist, we could draw on this as well (and this is an area that the city would like some help with as well). Have city master plan as well, it incorporates the climate action plan, this must be complied with, not optional.
  - Ibrahim - engage closely with the law department because planning board has strict rules about compliance with scope restrictions - need to not go outside of the scope allowed, CEAC involvement needs to follow whatever rules are there.
  - Beverly is GBC member, so can access their resources and information about LEED for cities.
  - Revisit this in September. Specifically reviewing Climate action Plan and LEED for City, and how CEAC can assist / contribute to planning board review.
  - Ibrahim - also an opportunity for CEAC to contribute/weigh in on energy projects. New permitting rule out that will have to be implemented. Opportunity from direct involvement in advisor role on clean energy projects coming to the city.
  - MAPC and DOER met with Beverly today and planning department and Ibrahim to talk about the energy permitting ordinances that Beverly will need to roll out, incorporate in existing zoning rules. Have finalized regulation and attachments he will forward to us, along with the slides from meeting today once they are available (don't have them yet).
  - City is also looking at CHARM facility. This effort is moving forward, starting with cardboard at the Stanley street facilities. Adding more in the spring. Plan being shared in community discussions regarding trash haul transition.
  - David - policy for vendors that build infrastructure (like fiber optic cable) in Beverly, such that when they install something it needs to also be removed by that vendor. New environmental purchasing policy does discuss end of life take back. Could be considered as part of procurement process.
- **CEAC plans for September and onward**
  - Jordan stepping down as chair, staying on as a member. Huge thanks to Jordan and appreciation for all that he has done.
  - Jordan's ideas - where are there opportunities for making the chair roles easier? Opportunities for dividing up some responsibilities: minutes (drafting / approving / posting), setting up meeting location, AV system in the library (try to keep hybrid set up for meetings). Chair needs to keep agenda setting, outreach to speakers, engaging with City Council liaisons.
  - Fred happy to provide support for specific responsibilities - meeting scheduling. (We do have the room book for third Wednesday for rest of the year except for November).
  - Go to City Council and give update on our work. Quick 5 minutes. (Can be done by non-chair members)
  - Can set the agenda as a group in the prior meeting.
  - Could alternate facilitators at the meeting (working through the meeting agenda) to help share the load.
  - Nancy nominates Kira as next CEAC chair, Tom seconded. Members unanimously vote in favor.
  - Sarah - she is limited in her participation to ensure there is no potential conflict of interest with her work. Still would like to attend and provide insight as she is able, but doesn't feel like she can be fully active as a member with her conflicts in place. She will stay on as a committee member until someone can step into her seat so that we have a full committee.
  - Amy may also step down if there is someone else who would be interested in joining, since she travels a lot and has to miss a lot of meetings.
  - Need to update CEAC website with who was mayoral appointment versus city council appointment - it alternates, and want to correct the information. (Jordan can track down this information.) City is working to revamp the website in next 6 months.
- **Thoughts for next year (Fred & others) -**
  - Possible CEAC work & focus areas:
    - Energy permitting processes
    - Planning board contributions - Climate Action Plan
    - State initiatives that are in place
    - Legislative proposals in play
    - Parking reform
    - Reviewing & Acting on Fleet assessment report
  - For Septembers agenda:
    - update on parking reform
    - Results from fleet assessment report (Jordan and Ibrahim)
    - Plan for planning board contributions
    - Process for updates to city hall
    - Update on state initiatives & legislation in play
    - CEAC - contribute to how to use the funding available to the city.

Jordan adjourned the meeting at 8:03 pm
